ai.description: *Eutropis rudis* reaches 12 cm snout-vent length. It is dark brown with a bronze sheen and a pale lateral stripe. Distinctive features include strongly keeled scales and a robust, cylindrical body.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eutropis rudis* is best distinguished by its strongly keeled dorsal scales, which give the body a rough, sandpaper-like texture compared to the smoother scales of other *Eutropis*.
ai.habitat: *Eutropis rudis* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically found in leaf litter or near streams at low to moderate elevations across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Rough Mabuya is primarily diurnal and often forages for insects among leaf litter, where its keeled scales provide effective camouflage against the forest floor.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis rudis* is ovoviviparous, producing litters of 3–9 young. In India, breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis rudis* is found in Northeast India, primarily within the humid forests of the Eastern Himalayas and Assam, ranging from lowlands up to 1,000 meters.
